QF.id: IV Strategies Using Interest Rate Derivatives_17

question.text: A hedge fund has a Rs. 100 crore bond portfolio with duration 7.5 years. It wants to completely hedge using bond futures whose per-contract value is Rs. 2,50,000 with duration 10 years. How many contracts should it sell?

explanation.text: The Logic: Using the duration-based hedge ratio (workbook pp. 164-165): Number of futures = (Portfolio value x Portfolio duration) / (Per-contract futures value x Futures duration) = (100,00,00,000 x 7.5) / (2,50,000 x 10) = 3,000 contracts. To hedge a bond portfolio against rising rates (falling bond prices), sell bond futures. The Trap: 4,000 uses portfolio duration in the denominator. 7,500 ignores futures duration. 2,000 uses the duration difference instead of the ratio. Note: Rs. 2,50,000 here is the per-contract futures value, which is what the duration-hedge formula requires.
